open_points.subject: Personal-data trust boundary
open_points.text: “Personal data — the customer's contact data (R0-06); readable by staff only (R0-09)” conflicts with “whatever [the operator] records or reads passes through its model provider”
open_points.question: Is the operator's model provider an expressly permitted recipient of customer contact data despite the staff-only rule, and which operator reads or writes may disclose which fields to it?
options: Treat the model provider as an accepted exception to staff-only visibility
Treat staff-only literally and prevent contact data from reaching the model provider
Limit the exception to specified fields or operator actions
open_points.default_guess: Treat the model provider as an accepted processor for data used by the agent, while keeping it unauthorized to call Registry directly.

open_points.subject: Direct access to the Registry store
open_points.text: “An agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read the store itself”
open_points.question: Is direct store access an authorized operator action, merely an acknowledged ability outside the product contract, or something storage permissions must prevent; and is direct writing always forbidden?
options: Authorized read-only operator path outside the API
Acknowledged host-level capability but not a supported product action
Store access must be restricted to Registry despite the agent's host access
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an acknowledged host-level capability, not a supported action, and require all mutations to use the API.

open_points.subject: Required and invalid instance configuration
open_points.text: “Service tokens, the staff credential, the artifact vocabulary (R0-08) and the frontend origin are the instance's configuration” and “a change takes effect when the instance restarts” do not say what happens when a value is absent, malformed or internally inconsistent
open_points.question: Which configuration entries are mandatory, may the vocabulary or service-token set be empty, and must Registry refuse to start when non-vocabulary configuration is missing or invalid?
options: All listed entries are mandatory and invalid configuration prevents startup
Permit an empty vocabulary or token set but require the staff credential and frontend origin
Allow omitted features and disable only the affected capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Validate configuration at startup, require the staff credential, allow empty service-token and artifact-vocabulary collections, and require a frontend origin only when browser access is enabled.

open_points.subject: Staff-credential replacement
open_points.text: “a replaced token stops working at that restart, with no overlap” specifies replacement for a token but not for the separately named staff credential
open_points.question: When the staff credential is replaced, does the old credential stop working at the same restart with no overlap, or is a different rotation rule intended?
options: Use the same restart boundary and no-overlap rule as service tokens
Allow an overlap period for old and new staff credentials
open_points.default_guess: Apply the same restart-boundary, no-overlap replacement rule to the staff credential.
